findings.body: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner is only true for OWNERs because isTeamAdmin already returns true for ADMIN/OWNER and is ANDed with isTeamOwner; a legitimate team admin is rejected with FORBIDDEN.
findings.failure_mode: Authorized admin users are incorrectly denied the add-guests action.
findings.impact: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner is only true for OWNERs because isTeamAdmin already returns true for ADMIN/OWNER and is ANDed with isTeamOwner; a legitimate team admin is rejected with FORBIDDEN.
findings.root_cause: Boolean AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner narrows authorization to owners only, contradicting the intended admin-or-owner semantics.
findings.suggested_fix: Combine the checks with `||` (or just use isTeamAdmin, which already covers owners) so admins are permitted as the name implies.
findings.title: Team-admin permission check requires OWNER, blocking admins
findings.trigger: A team ADMIN (not OWNER) who is neither the organizer nor an attendee attempts to add guests to a team booking.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch at lines 46-48 shows `isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Repository context confirms isTeamAdmin returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER roles (L270: OR [{role:ADMIN},{role:OWNER}]), while isTeamOwner only returns true for OWNER (L292: role:OWNER). The AND logic means only OWNERs satisfy both conditions, blocking legitimate ADMINs despite the variable name suggesting otherwise.

findings.body: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased but `guest` is not normalized, so mixed-case blacklisted addresses pass the filter and get added as attendees, defeating the blacklist.
findings.failure_mode: Blacklist enforcement is bypassed by case variation.
findings.impact: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased but `guest` is not normalized, so mixed-case blacklisted addresses pass the filter and get added as attendees, defeating the blacklist.
findings.root_cause: Only one side of the equality is case-normalized, so case-variant blacklisted emails are not matched.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare `guest.toLowerCase()` against the lowercased blacklist entries.
findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against lowercased list
findings.trigger: A blacklisted email is submitted with any uppercase characters (e.g. Blocked@Example.com) while BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS stores it lowercased.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 70-77 show blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased via .map(email => email.toLowerCase()), but the filter at line 77 compares with `guest` directly without lowercasing. Case-variant emails bypass the blacklist check.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorized admin users are incorrectly denied the add-guests action.
raw_findings.impact: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner is only true for OWNERs because isTeamAdmin already returns true for ADMIN/OWNER and is ANDed with isTeamOwner; a legitimate team admin is rejected with FORBIDDEN.
raw_findings.root_cause: Boolean AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner narrows authorization to owners only, contradicting the intended admin-or-owner semantics.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Combine the checks with `||` (or just use isTeamAdmin, which already covers owners) so admins are permitted as the name implies.
raw_findings.title: Team-admin permission check requires OWNER, blocking admins
raw_findings.trigger: A team ADMIN (not OWNER) who is neither the organizer nor an attendee attempts to add guests to a team booking.

raw_findings.body: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased but `guest` is not normalized, so mixed-case blacklisted addresses pass the filter and get added as attendees, defeating the blacklist.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Blacklist enforcement is bypassed by case variation.
raw_findings.impact: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased but `guest` is not normalized, so mixed-case blacklisted addresses pass the filter and get added as attendees, defeating the blacklist.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only one side of the equality is case-normalized, so case-variant blacklisted emails are not matched.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compare `guest.toLowerCase()` against the lowercased blacklist entries.
raw_findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against lowercased list
raw_findings.trigger: A blacklisted email is submitted with any uppercase characters (e.g. Blocked@Example.com) while BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS stores it lowercased.

raw_findings.body: The actual error object `err` is discarded and only a static string is written via console.log, so operators cannot diagnose why guest-notification emails failed while the mutation still reports success.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent loss of diagnostic information on email failures.
raw_findings.impact: The actual error object `err` is discarded and only a static string is written via console.log, so operators cannot diagnose why guest-notification emails failed while the mutation still reports success.
raw_findings.root_cause: Catch block ignores the error variable and uses console.log rather than the structured logger used elsewhere.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Log the caught `err` with the project logger (e.g. logger.error) instead of a bare console.log that drops the error.
raw_findings.title: Email send failure is silently swallowed without error detail
raw_findings.trigger: sendAddGuestsEmails throws (e.g. mailer misconfiguration or template render error).

raw_findings.body: Using the array index as key causes React to reuse input DOM nodes across shifted items, which can misplace focus/uncontrolled internal state of EmailField when entries are inserted or removed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect DOM/state reconciliation when the email list is mutated.
raw_findings.impact: Using the array index as key causes React to reuse input DOM nodes across shifted items, which can misplace focus/uncontrolled internal state of EmailField when entries are inserted or removed.
raw_findings.root_cause: Index-based keys do not track item identity across insertions/removals.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a stable key derived from the field identity (or generate a persistent id per row) instead of the array index.
raw_findings.title: MultiEmail list uses array index as React key
raw_findings.trigger: User removes an email from the middle of the list via onClickAddon, shifting subsequent items' indices.

raw_findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails treats any attendee whose email is in `guests` as newly added and sends them the AttendeeScheduledEmail; an already-existing attendee is thus re-notified as a brand-new guest instead of receiving the guests-added notification.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect email variant sent to pre-existing attendees.
raw_findings.impact: sendAddGuestsEmails treats any attendee whose email is in `guests` as newly added and sends them the AttendeeScheduledEmail; an already-existing attendee is thus re-notified as a brand-new guest instead of receiving the guests-added notification.
raw_findings.root_cause: newGuests is derived from the unfiltered input rather than the filtered uniqueGuests used for the DB insert.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `uniqueGuests` (the actually added set) instead of the raw `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails.
raw_findings.title: Guest emails sent using raw input instead of actually-added guests
raw_findings.trigger: A submitted guest email matches an existing attendee (filtered out of uniqueGuests) but remains in the raw `guests` array.

finding.body: Using the array index as key causes React to reuse input DOM nodes across shifted items, which can misplace focus/uncontrolled internal state of EmailField when entries are inserted or removed.

finding.impact: Using the array index as key causes React to reuse input DOM nodes across shifted items, which can misplace focus/uncontrolled internal state of EmailField when entries are inserted or removed.

finding.title: MultiEmail list uses array index as React key
finding.trigger: User removes an email from the middle of the list via onClickAddon, shifting subsequent items' indices.
finding.verifier_reason: Using array index as React key is a known anti-pattern but the claim of misplaced focus/state is speculative. The EmailField receives explicit value prop and onChange handler making it controlled. The impact is not concretely proven from the patch evidence.
